title: The operator deploys an environment from the goal and sees where it went
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-5d30948435524c6fa2789e1c033aafe7 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-3706b7e7bb8741d88105f42c25166ea0) and child 2 (task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5). PROOF ROW: owns the UI, the Playwright journey, the live drive and the docs (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: a Deployments card on the opened goal (per environment: target, last deploy sha / time / url / status, Deploy arm/confirm), the release-receipt row on Runs, Needs-you listing a goal ready to deploy after preview/release, and the live local deploy.

THE CARD MUST NOT INVITE AN ACCIDENTAL PRODUCTION DEPLOY. PREVIEW and PRODUCTION sit on the same card, and the destructive one is a click away from the safe one. Arm/confirm (the PUBLISH card's pattern) is the minimum; make the environment being deployed unmistakable in the confirm step, and show whether a release decision exists for a PRODUCTION deploy so the operator sees what child 2 recorded rather than discovering it in a receipt afterwards.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb: the pattern to model is apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-publish.tsx (141 lines, testids cr.publish.root/landed/state/link/unoffered) with publish-port.ts (22 lines) spending the offer through offer-wire's `spendOffer`. Needs-you is needs-you-model.ts (its NEEDS_YOU_KINDS roster at :28) plus needs-you.tsx. Note other rows are extending both: task-a988ca1c adds PLAN_REJECTED and task-33ceae56 adds a preview card - expect a rebase on that roster.
definitionOfDone: The Deployments card renders per environment - target, last deploy sha, time, url and status - with a Deploy arm/confirm modelled on the PUBLISH card, dispatching child 2's kinds through offer-wire `spendOffer` (no second decision wire).

THE CONFIRM STEP NAMES THE ENVIRONMENT UNMISTAKABLY, and a PRODUCTION deploy shows whether a release decision exists on the goal. Assert both: PREVIEW and PRODUCTION share a card, and the operator must not be able to deploy production believing they clicked preview.

The card is ABSENT (not a dead button) when the daemon offers no deploy, and a missing target renders DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING as words with a way to set one. All four refusal codes render VERBATIM, with DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED carrying the tool's last stderr line so a failure is diagnosable from the browser.
Runs shows deploy receipts and Needs-you lists a goal ready to deploy, then stops listing it once deployed - assert appearance AND disappearance.

A Playwright journey against a REAL daemon (with a fake docker port behind the daemon) covers target -> deploy -> url; `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted. Control-room fixtures are REAL daemon frames from that run.

LIVE DRIVE: the PREVIEW environment deployed LOCALLY with docker for UnAI or the scaffold app - the receipt and a curl of the health URL (status and body) in a row comment under ~4500 chars. If docker is unavailable on the lane, record DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE verbatim rather than a fabricated deploy.

The runbook gains a 'Deploy' section and README's Stage 2 status is updated to the measured state, with the live drive's date. Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: PRODUCTION IS ONE CLICK FROM PREVIEW ON THIS CARD. The confirm step names the environment unmistakably; this is the row's one safety property.
THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD: an infrastructure defect is child 1's, a deploy-effect defect is child 2's. Comment there and report_blocked.
REUSE the PUBLISH card's arm/confirm shape and offer-wire `spendOffer`. A second decision wire is a design regression.
NEEDS_YOU_KINDS is being extended by two other rows concurrently (task-a988ca1c, task-33ceae56) - rebase, do not delete a peer's entry.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check any new testid namespace is free; keep every production file under 250 lines.

implementationPlan.description:
READ EVERY PRODUCER'S SHIPPED SHAPE. NO EDITS. Five of six dependencies were unmet when this plan was written, so nothing below may be assumed - the previous plan was handed back for exactly that.

For each, confirm it landed and RECORD THE ACTUAL SHAPE you will consume:
- task-c9e76f53 (the Deployments card): `git grep -n "cr\.deploy\|goal-deployments" -- apps/control-room/src`. Its testids and per-environment layout are what step 3's journey drives.
- task-2cedb26a (the per-goal deploy offer): confirm the affordance read emits `targetAggregateId === "deploy:<goalId>"`. The card matches that exact string; a project-targeted offer renders nothing.
- task-79f8c7c0 (`productionDeployPorts.target`): confirm it is no longer `() => null`. ALSO CHECK `releaseDecision` - it was stubbed identically at deploy-command.ts:91 and DoD 2 requires the confirm to SHOW whether a release decision exists. If it is still null, DoD 2 cannot be satisfied in production: say so and report rather than asserting against an injected port.
- task-c3291fe0 (the deployment-state read): its route and decoded shape feed the card and Runs.
- task-4d77ba04 (target binding from the browser): without it there is no way to reach a bound state through the UI, which step 3's journey needs.
- task-cf2d91d9 (the fake docker seam): confirm the composition accepts it, and note that a journey on it proves COMPOSITION AND DISPATCH, not that a container ran.

If any is absent, `moe.report_blocked` with `blockedOnTaskIds`. Do NOT mock a producer, do NOT hand-build a daemon frame, and do NOT narrow a DoD clause to what the missing producer would have supplied.

Also re-read the contended files at HEAD: README.md and docs/agent-stack-runbook.md (four rows), needs-you-model.ts and needs-you.tsx (three rows).

NEEDS-YOU AND RUNS (DoD 4) - the two cross-goal surfaces this row owns.

NEEDS-YOU: a goal ready to deploy is listed, and STOPS being listed once deployed. DoD 4 requires BOTH - assert appearance AND disappearance. An item that appears correctly but never clears leaves a permanent false to-do, and a test asserting only appearance stays green through it.
Adding a kind to `NEEDS_YOU_KINDS` (needs-you-model.ts) forces TWO exhaustive `Record<NeedsYouKind, …>` maps - `KIND_ORDER` in the model and `KIND_EYEBROW` in needs-you.tsx - because `NeedsYouKind` is derived from the tuple. needs-you.tsx imports only the TYPE, so a symbol grep never names it; that coupling is why this is a two-file change.
THREE ROWS ARE EDITING THESE FILES CONCURRENTLY (task-6ec875f4, task-85895a88, task-f008f29a). Rebase onto their entries; never delete a peer's roster member to clean your diff. Do NOT assert a hard count of roster members - a frozen count reds on a peer landing rather than on a defect.
KIND_ORDER is a priority, not a formality: a deploy-ready goal sits somewhere relative to PLAN_APPROVAL, ESCALATION, GATE_1 and READY_TO_CLOSE. Choose deliberately and say why.

RUNS: add the deploy receipt's operator words to apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activity-words.ts, modelling the existing `"internal.repository.publish_receipt": "recorded the publish"` entry. A DEPLOYED and a REFUSED receipt must NOT read the same - a refused deploy is the interesting event, and a feed rendering both as "deployed" hides exactly what an operator is scanning for. ASCII only, no apostrophe (the scheduler boundary scan reds on an apostrophe in JSX).

THE JOURNEY (DoD 5) - a new spec under tests/e2e/control-room/, against a REAL daemon.

HARNESS: `withDaemonBackedControlRoom` / `DaemonLane` from ./daemon-ports.js. Drive the bare `lane.baseUrl` - main.tsx:101 serves the legacy shell only for `?v1=1`, so a journey clicking `cr.liveboard.*` re-proves the old dev board and leaves the shipped surface untested. Seat any dispatch recorder BEFORE the first click: a card's dispatch report lives only until the next surface poll re-keys the card (board-chain.spec.ts:26-33).

COVER target -> deploy -> url: bind a target through the browser (task-4d77ba04's control), arm and confirm a PREVIEW deploy on the Deployments card, and assert the resulting url is rendered. Then assert the receipt row appears in Runs and Needs-you stops listing the goal - the two surfaces step 2 owns, proven through the real path.

USE THE FAKE DOCKER SEAM from task-cf2d91d9 and SAY WHAT IT PROVES. A journey on that seam proves the daemon composed and dispatched correctly; it does NOT prove a container ran, an image was built, or a URL served real bytes. Write that distinction into the spec's header and the completion record. DoD 5 asks for a journey against a real daemon, and that is what this is - a real daemon with a faked container runtime, stated plainly rather than implied.

Control-room fixtures are REAL daemon frames captured from that run, not hand-written objects; say how they were captured.

TEARDOWN in a `finally`: the lane, the daemon child, the fake seam's recorded state and any temp directory - released on the throwing path too (epic rail 4).

Quote the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line.

THE LIVE DRIVE (DoD 6) - and this is the clause where the fake seam must NOT be used.

Deploy the PREVIEW environment LOCALLY with REAL docker - the scaffold app or UnAI - and record the receipt plus a curl of the health URL (status AND body) in a row comment under ~4500 chars. Step 3's journey proves dispatch; this proves a container actually served, and the two are not interchangeable.

PREVIEW ONLY. Do not drive a PRODUCTION deploy: production is one click from preview on this card and a live production deploy is not this row's to perform.

DOCKER WAS 29.6.2 ON THIS HOST AT 2026-09-06 but has been absent before - it was missing for most of 2026-09-05 and parked task-3706b7e7's DoD 3. If it is unavailable when you reach this step, record `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE` VERBATIM together with what WAS proven (the journey, the composed dispatch), and say plainly that no container ran. That is a complete, honest outcome and DoD 6 anticipates it - a fabricated receipt is not.

STOP WHAT YOU START (epic rail 4): the container, the image and any port this drive opens are torn down when it ends, including when it fails. Record the teardown commands and their output, and `docker ps -a` afterwards.

No credential, no registry URL with embedded userinfo, no connection string in the comment, the transcript or a screenshot (epic rail 3). Check before pasting.

Record the DATE - step 5's docs are dated to it.

DOCS (DoD 7, first half). Both files are CONTENDED - README.md by five rows and docs/agent-stack-runbook.md by four. Re-read HEAD immediately before editing and rebase; never regenerate either from an older copy.

`docs/agent-stack-runbook.md` gains a Deploy section: binding a target, the arm/confirm on the Deployments card, what a PRODUCTION deploy shows about the release decision, and what each refusal code means to an operator. Write what the drive actually did.

`README.md` Stage 2 status - update for DEPLOYMENT ONLY. docs/VISION.md:141 lists Stage 2 as "repository bootstrapping; infrastructure generation; preview and production deployment; secrets and environment management; database migrations; monitoring, backup, and rollback; release evidence". The other items belong to other rows and must NOT be marked shipped here. Overstating Stage 2 retires questions no one has answered.

STATE WHAT WAS PROVEN AND HOW. If step 4's live drive ran, say a container served. If it recorded DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE, say the machinery is verified and a live container deploy is pending a docker host. If DoD 2's release-decision display could not be satisfied because `releaseDecision` is still `() => null` (step 1), say that too - a runbook describing a citation the product cannot produce is worse than one that omits it.

If a doc needed no change, name the files you READ to reach that conclusion.

GATES (DoD 7, second half). Each leg standalone, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING, and `pnpm --filter <pkg>` exits 0 with "No projects matched the filters" for a name that is not a workspace package.
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` - this row's primary evidence; the Needs-you and Runs edits live there.
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test:e2e:browser` - the journey's lane.
State explicitly that root `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** file, so the control-room leg carries the apps/** claim.

Respect the host's one-full-suite-at-a-time rule (GATE START/END in #general); prefer filtered legs. Expect foreign timeout reds from `mtkbtsvc` handle exhaustion and attribute them by path rather than re-running the suite, which degrades every other seat's gate.

PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE: repo-wide failures at the merge-base, at HEAD, subtract, intersect with this row's owned paths; complete only when that intersection is EMPTY. Disclose any foreign red verbatim with its failing file paths.

CONTENDED-FILE CHECK before the final commit: re-read needs-you-model.ts, needs-you.tsx, README.md and docs/agent-stack-runbook.md at HEAD. If a peer landed while you worked, rebase onto their change rather than reverting it.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW before `moe.complete_task`.

WHAT THIS ROW CLAIMS vs WHAT IT PROVED - the sharpest question here, because two different proofs are involved:
- Does any completion sentence read as "a deploy worked" when only dispatch was proven? Step 3's journey runs on a fake docker seam and step 4's drive may have been unavailable. Separate the two claims explicitly.
- Does DoD 2's release-decision display actually work in production, or only against an injected port? `releaseDecision` was `() => null` at deploy-command.ts:91 when this plan was written. If task-79f8c7c0 did not take it, say so rather than letting a green component test stand in for it.

THE SURFACES:
- Does the Needs-you item clear on a FAILED deploy, or only a successful one? A refused deploy that clears the to-do hides work the operator still owes; one that never clears trains them to ignore the list. Assert which ships.
- Does Runs distinguish a REFUSED deploy from a DEPLOYED one at a glance?
- Does the confirm still name the environment after a surface poll re-keys the card mid-incident?
- Did a peer's roster entry survive your rebase in needs-you-model.ts and needs-you.tsx?

SECURITY AND CLEANUP:
- Any credential, registry URL with embedded userinfo, or connection string in a rendered string, log line, screenshot or the live-drive comment? Epic rail 3.
- After the suite and the drive: `docker ps -a` and a port check, quoted. Nothing this row started may survive (epic rail 4).

MUTATION DRILL: `git status --porcelain` the exact paths FIRST. The spec is NEW and untracked, so `git diff` certifies nothing for it - back it up out of tree under %TEMP% suffixed by your worker id and prove the restore by SHA256 in a SEPARATE call. The Needs-you, Runs and doc files are TRACKED, so `git diff` is valid there.
